transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Thanks for seeing me, doctor. Ever since I witnessed a terrible freeway crash about three weeks ago, I feel constantly on edge, like I’m scanning for danger all the time and can’t relax, especially when I’m out driving.
Have you been experiencing any vivid flashbacks, nightmares, or sudden, unwanted memories of the crash since it happened?

Yes, during the day I'll suddenly see the injured driver's bloody face and hear the crunch of metal, which makes my heart race and completely derails whatever I'm doing. At night, I bolt awake around three or four in the morning from these half-dreams of screeching brakes and just can't get back to sleep.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid driving, certain roads, or anything else that reminds you of the crash?

Yes, I've been completely avoiding the freeway by taking complicated side-street routes and even rearranging my entire work schedule to steer clear of it. I also had to leave a community festival early the other day because just hearing sirens in the distance made me feel too overwhelmed to stay.
Have you also felt emotionally numb, detached from your loved ones, or unable to experience positive emotions like happiness since the crash?

Yes, I've been feeling really flat and disconnected from everything. At my kid's soccer game when everyone was cheering for the win, I felt like I was just watching it on TV and couldn't tap into any real joy at all.
Since the crash happened about three weeks ago, have these symptoms been present nearly every day, and do you feel they are staying just as intense or even worsening?

Yes, it's been happening every single day since the crash three weeks ago. It hasn't gotten any better at all, and the intensity is just as strong now as it was right after it happened. I'm constantly exhausted because I just can't find any relief from this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) following a severe traumatic event (witnessing a horrific freeway crash three weeks ago). The patient exhibits characteristic symptoms across all major clusters: intrusive re-experiencing (vivid flashbacks, nightmares, and physiological reactivity), active avoidance of trauma-related reminders (avoiding freeways and sirens), emotional numbing/detachment, and persistent hyperarousal (constant vigilance and sleep disturbance), causing significant functional impairment.
